questions.answer: Differentiate \(y=\cos x\) once to get \(y'=-\sin x\). Differentiate again to get \(y''=-\cos x\). Substitute into the equation: \(y''+y=-\cos x+\cos x=0\). Therefore \(y=\cos x\) solves the differential equation.
Integrate once: \(y'=\int 6x\,dx=3x^2+C_1\). Integrate again: \(y=\int(3x^2+C_1)\,dx=x^3+C_1x+C_2\). Therefore the general solution is \(y=x^3+C_1x+C_2\).

Assume \(y=e^{rx}\), giving the characteristic equation \(r^2-5r+6=0\). Factor: \((r-2)(r-3)=0\), so \(r=2\) or \(r=3\). With two distinct real roots, the general solution is \(y=C_1e^{2x}+C_2e^{3x}\).

Use the trial solution \(y=e^{rx}\), giving \(r^2+4=0\). Thus \(r^2=-4\), so \(r=\pm2i\). For complex roots \(\pm bi\), the real solution is \(y=C_1\cos bx+C_2\sin bx\). Therefore \(y=C_1\cos 2x+C_2\sin 2x\).
The characteristic equation is \(r^2-4r+4=0\). Factoring gives \((r-2)^2=0\), so \(r=2\) is a repeated root. For a repeated root, the general solution is \(y=(C_1+C_2x)e^{2x}\).

The general solution of \(y''+y=0\) is \(y=C_1\cos x+C_2\sin x\). Then \(y'= -C_1\sin x+C_2\cos x\). Applying \(y(0)=2\) gives \(C_1=2\). Applying \(y'(0)=3\) gives \(C_2=3\). Therefore \(y=2\cos x+3\sin x\).

Assume a solution of the form \(y=e^{rx}\). Then \(y'=re^{rx}\) and \(y''=r^2e^{rx}\). Substituting gives \(2r^2e^{rx}+3re^{rx}-5e^{rx}=0\). Since \(e^{rx}\ne0\), the characteristic equation is \(2r^2+3r-5=0\).

The characteristic equation is \(r^2+2r+5=0\). Using the quadratic formula, \(r=(-2\pm\sqrt{4-20})/2=-1\pm2i\). For roots \(\alpha\pm\beta i\), the solution is \(e^{\alpha x}(C_1\cos\beta x+C_2\sin\beta x)\). Therefore \(y=e^{-x}(C_1\cos2x+C_2\sin2x)\).

questions.prompt: Find a particular solution to \(y''-y=e^x\) using the trial form \(y_p=Ax e^x\).
questions.answer: Because \(e^x\) solves the homogeneous equation, use \(y_p=Ax e^x\). Then \(y_p'=A(e^x+xe^x)=A(1+x)e^x\), and \(y_p''=A(2+x)e^x\). Substitute: \(y_p''-y_p=A(2+x)e^x-Axe^x=2Ae^x\). Set \(2Ae^x=e^x\), so \(A=1/2\). Thus \(y_p=\frac{x}{2}e^x\).

questions.prompt: For \(y''+9y=0\), state the general solution and identify the oscillation frequency in the argument of sine and cosine.
questions.answer: The characteristic equation is \(r^2+9=0\), so \(r=\pm3i\). Therefore the general solution is \(y=C_1\cos3x+C_2\sin3x\). The number multiplying \(x\) inside sine and cosine is \(3\), so the angular frequency in the argument is \(3\).
